# Player

Someone on the server: a `Living`, with everything living entities have, and more. A handle is a UUID, so keeping one is fine: if they leave, its methods answer `nil` or `false` rather than erroring, and work again when they come back. `nf.players.get` hands out handles to people who are offline too. Their real inventory is numbered: the hotbar 0 to 8, the rest of the main inventory 9 to 35, armour 36 (feet), 37 (legs), 38 (chest) and 39 (head), the offhand 40, then body armour 41 and a saddle 42 (what the game keeps there for any entity).

A handle: call its methods with a colon, `player:method()`.

It is a [Living](living.md), which is an [Entity](entity.md): it has every method and event of those classes too (its own replace any of the same name), and goes wherever a `Living` or an `Entity` is taken.


## Events

What `player:on(event, handler)` listens for. See [Events](events.md) for how events work.

| Event | Payload | Cancellable | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `join` | [PlayerJoinEvent](events.md#playerjoinevent) |  | A player joined the server. Assign `event.message` to change what everyone is told, or `nil` to say nothing. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_join")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `message`. |
| `quit` | [PlayerQuitEvent](events.md#playerquitevent) |  | A player left. Assign `event.message` to change what everyone is told, or `nil` to say nothing. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_quit")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `message`. |
| `chat` | [PlayerChatEvent](events.md#playerchatevent) | yes | A player is saying something in chat. `event:cancel()` stops anyone seeing it; assign `event.message` to change what they said, or `event.format` to change how the line looks. Handlers run on the main thread while the chat waits for them, so keep them quick. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_chat")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `message`, `format`. |
| `interact` | [PlayerInteractEvent](events.md#playerinteractevent) | yes | A player clicked a block or the air (not an entity), once for each hand the game asks about. `event:cancel()` stops it: no door opens, nothing is placed or used. A right click with an item goes on to `player_use_item` unless it was cancelled. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_interact")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `interact_entity` | [PlayerInteractEntityEvent](events.md#playerinteractentityevent) | yes | A player right-clicked an entity that isn't part of a centity (those are `centity_click`): after the entity's `interact` and the player's `interact_entity`. `event:cancel()` stops what the click would do. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_interact_entity")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `move` | [PlayerMoveEvent](events.md#playermoveevent) | yes | A player moved into another block: walking, swimming, flying, falling, riding. Only moves that change block are heard, not every step or turn of the head, and teleports are `player_teleport` instead. `event:cancel()` puts them back where they were. The server only watches moves while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_move")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `teleport` | [PlayerTeleportEvent](events.md#playerteleportevent) | yes | A player is being teleported: a command, a script, an ender pearl, a portal. `event:cancel()` keeps them where they are; assign `event.to` to send them somewhere else. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_teleport")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `to`. |
| `change_world` | [PlayerChangeWorldEvent](events.md#playerchangeworldevent) |  | A player arrived in another world: through a portal, or teleported there. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_change_world")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `death` | [PlayerDeathEvent](events.md#playerdeathevent) |  | A player died: before `nf.on("entity_death")` hears the same death. Assign `event.message` to change what everyone is told (or `nil` for nothing), `event.keep_inventory` to let them keep what they carry, and `event.drops` to change what falls. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_death")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `message`, `keep_inventory`, `drops`. |
| `respawn` | [PlayerRespawnEvent](events.md#playerrespawnevent) |  | A player is coming back after dying, or after leaving the end. Assign `event.location` to bring them back somewhere else. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_respawn")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `location`. |
| `drop_item` | [PlayerItemEvent](events.md#playeritemevent) | yes | A player is dropping an item from their inventory. `event:cancel()` keeps it in their inventory. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_drop_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `pickup_item` | [PlayerPickupItemEvent](events.md#playerpickupitemevent) | yes | A player is picking up a dropped item. `event:cancel()` leaves it lying there (it is asked again while they stand on it). Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_pickup_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `use_item` | [PlayerUseItemEvent](events.md#playeruseitemevent) | yes | A player right-clicked with an item, on a block or the air, after `player_interact`: starting to eat or drink, drawing a bow, throwing a pearl, emptying a bucket, placing a block. `event:cancel()` stops the item being used, but not what the click does to the block (a door still opens). Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_use_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `consume_item` | [PlayerItemEvent](events.md#playeritemevent) | yes | A player finished eating or drinking something. `event:cancel()` stops it: the item stays and does nothing. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_consume_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `swap_hands` | [PlayerEvent](events.md#playerevent) | yes | A player pressed the key that swaps the items in their hands. `event:cancel()` leaves them where they are, so the key can be used for something else. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_swap_hands")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `sneak` | [PlayerSneakEvent](events.md#playersneakevent) |  | A player started or stopped sneaking. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_sneak")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `command` | [PlayerCommandEvent](events.md#playercommandevent) | yes | A player typed a command (any command: Minecraft's, a plugin's or a script's), before it runs. `event:cancel()` stops it running. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_command")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `input` | [PlayerInputEvent](events.md#playerinputevent) |  | A player's movement keys changed: what they hold down now, as their game sends it (forward, back, left, right, jump, sneak, sprint), whether or not they can move. For steering something they ride or controlling a centity. The server only watches input while something listens, so it costs nothing otherwise. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_input")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `change_slot` | [PlayerChangeSlotEvent](events.md#playerchangeslotevent) | yes | A player picked another hotbar slot: a number key or the scroll wheel. `event:cancel()` keeps the slot they had. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_change_slot")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `swing` | [PlayerSwingEvent](events.md#playerswingevent) | yes | A player swung an arm: every left click, on a block, an entity or the air, and some right clicks. The one way to hear a left click on the air. `event:cancel()` stops others seeing the swing, but not what the click does. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_swing")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `sprint` | [PlayerSprintEvent](events.md#playersprintevent) |  | A player started or stopped sprinting. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_sprint")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `fly` | [PlayerFlyEvent](events.md#playerflyevent) | yes | A player started or stopped flying (in creative, or where `set_can_fly` lets them). `event:cancel()` keeps them as they were. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_fly")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `jump` | [PlayerJumpEvent](events.md#playerjumpevent) | yes | A player jumped. `event:cancel()` puts them back where they jumped from. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_jump")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `change_game_mode` | [PlayerChangeGameModeEvent](events.md#playerchangegamemodeevent) | yes | A player's game mode is changing: a command, a script, or the server. `event:cancel()` keeps the one they have. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_change_game_mode")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `change_food` | [PlayerChangeFoodEvent](events.md#playerchangefoodevent) | yes | A player's food level is changing: going down as they get hungry, up as they eat. `event:cancel()` keeps it as it is; assign `event.food` to set it to another level. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_change_food")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `food`. |
| `gain_experience` | [PlayerGainExperienceEvent](events.md#playergainexperienceevent) |  | A player is getting experience points: picking up orbs, or from a script or command. Assign `event.amount` to give another amount (0 for none). Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_gain_experience")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `amount`. |
| `change_level` | [PlayerChangeLevelEvent](events.md#playerchangelevelevent) |  | A player's experience level changed, up or down. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_change_level")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `kick` | [PlayerKickEvent](events.md#playerkickevent) | yes | A player is being kicked: by a command, a plugin or a script, or by the server (flying, timing out, a bad packet). `event:cancel()` keeps them on the server; assign `event.text` to change what their screen says, or `event.message` to change what everyone is told (`nil` for nothing). Leaving then goes on to `player_quit`. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_kick")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `text`, `message`. |
| `complete_advancement` | [PlayerAdvancementEvent](events.md#playeradvancementevent) |  | A player completed an advancement (or a recipe was unlocked for them: those are advancements too, under `minecraft:recipes/`). Assign `event.message` to change what everyone is told, or `nil` to say nothing. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_complete_advancement")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `message`. |
| `stop_using_item` | [PlayerStopUsingItemEvent](events.md#playerstopusingitemevent) |  | A player let go of an item they were using before it finished: a bow or crossbow drawn, a shield raised, a spyglass, food or a potion part-eaten. `event.ticks` says how long they held it. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_break_item")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `open_inventory` | [PlayerInventoryEvent](events.md#playerinventoryevent) | yes | A player is opening a vanilla inventory: a chest, a furnace, a crafting table, a villager's trades, a horse's. Not one of the project's menus: those are `menu_open`. `event:cancel()` keeps it closed. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_open_inventory")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `close_inventory` | [PlayerInventoryEvent](events.md#playerinventoryevent) |  | A player closed a vanilla inventory (not one of the project's menus: those are `menu_close`), or left the server with it open. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_close_inventory")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |
| `craft` | [PlayerCraftEvent](events.md#playercraftevent) | yes | A player is taking what they crafted out of the result slot (with shift, as many as they can make). `event:cancel()` leaves it there and keeps the ingredients. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_craft")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. |

Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_prepare_craft")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `result`. |

Assign `event.result` to make something else (or `nil` for nothing), and `event.cost` to change how many levels it takes. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_prepare_anvil")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `result`, `cost`. |

Assign `event.result` to make something else, or `nil` for nothing. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_prepare_smithing")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `result`. |
| `prepare_grindstone` | [PlayerPrepareGrindstoneEvent](events.md#playerpreparegrindstoneevent) |  | What is in a grindstone changed, and the game is working out the result. Assign `event.result` to make something else, or `nil` for nothing. Only this player's: heard before `nf.on("player_prepare_grindstone")`, with the same event, so `event:stop()` keeps it from there. Bubbles. Writable: `result`. |
| `enchant_item` | [PlayerEnchantItemEvent](events.md#playerenchantitemevent) | yes | A player is enchanting an item at an enchanting table. `event:cancel()` stops it: nothing is enchanted or spent. ## `player:name()`

Their name, as they have it now (a player can change theirs between visits).

**Returns** `string`

## `player:display_name()`

What chat and other plugins call them, as MiniMessage: their name unless something changed it. `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `Text?`

## `player:set_display_name(text)`

Changes what chat calls them, until they leave. Their real name, and what's above their head, stay.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Text` | MiniMessage. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:send_message(text)`

Sends them a chat line only they see.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Text` | MiniMessage, like `"<green>Done!"`. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:send_actionbar(text)`

Shows a line above their hotbar for a couple of seconds.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Text` | MiniMessage. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:send_title(title, subtitle?, options?)`

Shows a big title in the middle of their screen, with a smaller line under it.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | `Text` | MiniMessage. |
| `subtitle` (optional) | `Text` | MiniMessage. Default none. |
| `options` (optional) | `TitleOptions` |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

```lua
player:send_title("<gold>Round 2", "<gray>Fight!", { stay = 40 })
```

## `player:clear_title()`

Takes a title off their screen.

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:play_sound(sound, options?)`

Plays a sound only they hear, where they are, following them. The same sounds `world:play_sound` takes: an unknown one is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sound` | `string` | A Minecraft sound (`"minecraft:ui.button.click"`) or one of the project's resource pack sounds (`"<pack>/<key>"`, like `"ui/click"`). |
| `options` (optional) | `SoundOptions` |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

```lua
player:play_sound("minecraft:ui.button.click", { pitch = 2 })
```

## `player:stop_sound(sound?)`

Stops a sound playing for them, or every sound when it's left out. An unknown sound is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sound` (optional) | `string` | The sound to stop. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:spawn_particle(particle, position, options?)`

Spawns particles only they see, in their world: `world:spawn_particle` with `viewers = { player }`, so `viewers` isn't an option here.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `particle` | `string` | A particle id: `"minecraft:happy_villager"`. |
| `position` | `Vec3` | Where, in their world. |
| `options` (optional) | `ParticleOptions` |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:run(command)`

Runs a command as them, with their permissions. The leading slash is optional.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `command` | `string` |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: Whether it ran.

## `player:has_permission(permission)`

Whether they have a permission node. `false` when they're offline.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `permission` | `string` |  |

**Returns** `boolean`

## `player:set_permission(permission, value)`

Grants them a permission node (`true`), or denies it (`false`), alongside whatever a permissions plugin gives them. It's kept with the project's other grants and given back every time they join, until `unset_permission`; it works while they're offline too. A package (every project is one) may only grant nodes its own `netherforge.json` lists under `allow.permissions`, held to the package whose code makes the call as `requires` is (each entry allows itself and everything under it: `"shop"` allows `shop` and `shop.vip`): anything else is an error, and grants a later edit no longer allows stop applying.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `permission` | `string` | The node: lowercase letters, digits, `_`, `-` and `.`, like `"shop.vip"`. |
| `value` | `boolean` | `true` grants it; `false` denies it. |

```lua
player:set_permission("shop.vip", true)
```

## `player:unset_permission(permission)`

Takes back a node `set_permission` granted or denied: they have it again only if something else gives it to them.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `permission` | `string` | The node. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when the project hadn't set it.

## `player:permissions()`

The nodes the project has set for them with `set_permission`, each to `true` (granted) or `false` (denied). Not every permission they have: `has_permission` answers that.

**Returns** `table<string, boolean>`

## `player:is_operator()`

Whether they're a server operator, online or not.

**Returns** `boolean`

## `player:game_mode()`

Their game mode, or `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `"survival"\|"creative"\|"adventure"\|"spectator"\|nil`

## `player:set_game_mode(game_mode)`

Changes their game mode.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `game_mode` | `"survival"\|"creative"\|"adventure"\|"spectator"` |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

## `player:food()`

How full they are, 0 to 20 (20 is a full bar), or `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `integer?`

## `player:set_food(food)`

Sets how full they are.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `food` | `integer` | 0 to 20. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

## `player:saturation()`

How long until they get hungry again, 0 up to their food level, or `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `number?`

## `player:set_saturation(saturation)`

Sets their saturation, up to their food level.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `saturation` | `number` |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

## `player:level()`

Their experience level, or `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `integer?`

## `player:set_level(level)`

Sets their experience level.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `level` | `integer` | At least 0. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

## `player:experience_progress()`

How far the experience bar is towards the next level, 0 to 1, or `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `number?`

## `player:set_experience_progress(progress)`

Moves the experience bar, keeping their level.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `progress` | `number` | 0 to 1. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

## `player:give_experience(points)`

Gives them experience points, as orbs would: their level goes up when the bar fills.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `points` | `integer` | At least 0. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:is_flying()`

Whether they're flying. `false` when they're offline.

**Returns** `boolean`

## `player:set_flying(flying)`

Starts or stops them flying. They have to be able to fly (`set_can_fly`) to start.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flying` | `boolean` |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

## `player:can_fly()`

Whether they may fly (double-tapping jump), as in creative. `false` when they're offline.

**Returns** `boolean`

## `player:set_can_fly(can_fly)`

Lets them fly, or not.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `can_fly` | `boolean` |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

## `player:walk_speed()`

How fast they walk, 0 to 1 (0.2 is normal), or `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `number?`

## `player:set_walk_speed(speed)`

Sets how fast they walk.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `speed` | `number` | −1 to 1; 0.2 is normal. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

## `player:fly_speed()`

How fast they fly, 0 to 1 (0.1 is normal), or `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `number?`

## `player:set_fly_speed(speed)`

Sets how fast they fly.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `speed` | `number` | −1 to 1; 0.1 is normal. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

## `player:is_sneaking()`

Whether they're sneaking. `false` when they're offline.

**Returns** `boolean`

## `player:is_sprinting()`

Whether they're sprinting. `false` when they're offline.

**Returns** `boolean`

## `player:locale()`

The language their game is set to, like `"en_us"`, or `nil` when they're offline. Right after they join it can still be the default until their game says.

**Returns** `string?`

## `player:ping()`

How long a message takes to reach them and come back, in milliseconds, as the server estimates it; `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `integer?`

## `player:kick(reason?)`

Disconnects them from the server.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `reason` (optional) | `Text` | What their screen says, MiniMessage. Default the server's own message. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:first_played()`

When they first joined this server, as Unix time in milliseconds (like `nf.server.unix_time()`), or `nil` for someone who never has (a handle from `nf.players.whitelisted()`, say).

**Returns** `integer?`

## `player:last_seen()`

When they were last on this server, as Unix time in milliseconds (like `nf.server.unix_time()`): now while they're online, `nil` for someone who never has been.

**Returns** `integer?`

```lua
local seen = player:last_seen()
if seen then
  local days = (nf.server.unix_time() - seen) // 86400000
  log(player:name(), "was here", days, "days ago")
end
```

## `player:is_banned()`

Whether they're banned from the server (by `ban`, `/ban` or anything else), and the ban hasn't run out.

**Returns** `boolean`

## `player:ban(options?)`

Bans them from the server: they can't join until it runs out or `unban`. Kicks them, with the reason, when they're online. Banning someone already banned replaces their ban.

*Needs `"requires": { "moderation": true }` in `netherforge.json`: without it, calling it is an error.*

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `options` (optional) | `BanOptions` |  |

```lua
player:ban({ reason = "Griefing", expires = nf.server.unix_time() + 7 * 86400000 })
```

## `player:unban()`

Lifts their ban.

*Needs `"requires": { "moderation": true }` in `netherforge.json`: without it, calling it is an error.*

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they weren't banned.

## `player:is_whitelisted()`

Whether they're on the server's whitelist (which only keeps people out while it's on: `nf.server.is_whitelist_enabled()`).

**Returns** `boolean`

## `player:set_whitelisted(whitelisted)`

Puts them on the server's whitelist, or takes them off. Taking someone online off doesn't kick them.

*Needs `"requires": { "moderation": true }` in `netherforge.json`: without it, calling it is an error.*

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `whitelisted` | `boolean` |  |

## `player:ender_chest()`

Their ender chest, as an `Inventory`, or `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `Inventory?`

## `player:held_item()`

What's in their main hand (the selected hotbar slot), or `nil` for nothing or when they're offline.

**Returns** `Item?`

## `player:set_held_item(item?)`

Puts an item in their main hand, or empties it. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have, is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` (optional) | `Item` | Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty it. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:off_hand_item()`

What's in their offhand, or `nil` for nothing or when they're offline.

**Returns** `Item?`

## `player:set_off_hand_item(item?)`

Puts an item in their offhand, or empties it.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` (optional) | `Item` | Leave it out (or `nil`) to empty it. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:held_slot()`

Which hotbar slot they have selected, 0 to 8, or `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `integer?`

## `player:set_held_slot(index)`

Selects a hotbar slot for them.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `index` | `integer` | 0 to 8. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` once it has gone (or while its chunk is unloaded).

## `player:give_item(item)`

Puts an item into their inventory, topping up matching stacks first, and drops what doesn't fit at their feet. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have, is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `item` | `Item` |  |

**Returns** `integer?`: How many were dropped at their feet: 0 when everything fitted. `nil` when they're offline.

```lua
player:give_item({ kind = "minecraft:gold_nugget", count = 5, data = { coin = true } })
```

## `player:discover_recipe(recipe)`

Puts a recipe in their recipe book (with the toast that says so). `false` when they're offline, already had it, or the server has no such recipe; a project recipe id the project doesn't have is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `recipe` | `string` | A project recipe's id (`"ruby_sword"`), or any recipe the server has by its namespaced id (`"minecraft:bread"`). |

**Returns** `boolean`

```lua
nf.on("player_join", function(event)
  event.player:discover_recipe("ruby_sword")
end)
```

## `player:undiscover_recipe(recipe)`

Takes a recipe out of their recipe book. They can still craft it. `false` when they're offline or didn't have it.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `recipe` | `string` | A project recipe's id (`"ruby_sword"`), or any recipe the server has by its namespaced id (`"minecraft:bread"`). |

**Returns** `boolean`

## `player:has_discovered_recipe(recipe)`

Whether a recipe is in their recipe book. `false` when they're offline.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `recipe` | `string` | A project recipe's id (`"ruby_sword"`), or any recipe the server has by its namespaced id (`"minecraft:bread"`). |

**Returns** `boolean`

## `player:grant_advancement(advancement, criterion?)`

Meets an advancement's criteria for them, as if they'd earned them: every criterion, or just `criterion`. Once the advancement is complete they get the toast, the chat line and its rewards, as when the game completes it.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `advancement` | `string` | One of the project's advancements (`"first_steps"`, `advancements/first_steps.json`; a bare id is the calling package's own), one a package exports (`"acme:quests"`), or one of the game's by its key (`"minecraft:story/mine_diamond"`). One the server doesn't have is an error; so is a project advancement added since the server started, until it restarts. |
| `criterion` (optional) | `string` | Only this criterion, by the name the advancement's file gives it. One it doesn't have is an error. Leave it out for every criterion. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline or had already met it.

```lua
player:grant_advancement("minecraft:story/mine_diamond")
-- One step of a quest of the project's own (advancements/treasure_hunter.json):
player:grant_advancement("treasure_hunter", "first")
```

## `player:revoke_advancement(advancement, criterion?)`

Takes an advancement back: every criterion of it, or just `criterion`.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `advancement` | `string` | One of the project's advancements (`"first_steps"`, `advancements/first_steps.json`; a bare id is the calling package's own), one a package exports (`"acme:quests"`), or one of the game's by its key (`"minecraft:story/mine_diamond"`). One the server doesn't have is an error; so is a project advancement added since the server started, until it restarts. |
| `criterion` (optional) | `string` | Only this criterion, by the name the advancement's file gives it. One it doesn't have is an error. Leave it out for every criterion. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline or hadn't met any of it.

## `player:has_advancement(advancement)`

Whether they've completed an advancement. `false` when they're offline.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `advancement` | `string` | One of the project's advancements (`"first_steps"`, `advancements/first_steps.json`; a bare id is the calling package's own), one a package exports (`"acme:quests"`), or one of the game's by its key (`"minecraft:story/mine_diamond"`). One the server doesn't have is an error; so is a project advancement added since the server started, until it restarts. |

**Returns** `boolean`

## `player:advancement_progress(advancement)`

How far they are with an advancement: the criteria they've met and those left. `nil` when they're offline.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `advancement` | `string` | One of the project's advancements (`"first_steps"`, `advancements/first_steps.json`; a bare id is the calling package's own), one a package exports (`"acme:quests"`), or one of the game's by its key (`"minecraft:story/mine_diamond"`). One the server doesn't have is an error; so is a project advancement added since the server started, until it restarts. |

**Returns** `AdvancementProgress?`

```lua
local progress = player:advancement_progress("minecraft:adventure/adventuring_time")
if progress then
  player:send_message(#progress.done .. " biomes, " .. #progress.remaining .. " to go")
end
```

## `player:item_cooldown(key)`

How many ticks are left before they can use an item again, or 0. `nil` when they're offline.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | An item kind (`"minecraft:ender_pearl"`), or a cooldown group an item's `cooldown` names. |

**Returns** `integer?`

## `player:set_item_cooldown(key, ticks)`

Makes them wait before using an item again, as an ender pearl does: every item of that kind, or every item in that cooldown group. Items whose own `cooldown` names another group aren't affected by their kind's.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `key` | `string` | An item kind, or a cooldown group: `"<namespace>:<name>"`. |
| `ticks` | `integer` | How long; 0 ends it. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:open_menu(menu, options?)`

Opens a menu for them: the shared window for a `shared` menu, otherwise a new window of their own, filled from the file (or from the template). Its script's body has run (for a new window) and its `open` handlers have heard it by the time this returns. A menu the project doesn't have is an error; a template that's gone opens nothing (`nil`).

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `menu` | `string\|MenuTemplate` | Its folder name under `menus/`, or a `MenuTemplate` from `nf.menus.create`. |
| `options` (optional) | `MenuOpenOptions` | What to open it with: `context` for the new window. A key it doesn't take is an error. |

**Returns** `Menu?`: The window, or `nil` when they're offline.

```lua
nf.commands.register("shop", { players_only = true }, function(event)
  event.player:open_menu("shop", { context = { discount = 0.1 } })
end)
```

## `player:menu()`

The project menu window they're looking at, or `nil` (nothing open, or a chest that isn't one of ours).

**Returns** `Menu?`

## `player:close_menu()`

Closes the project menu they have open. Anything else on their screen (a chest, their own inventory) stays open.

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline or have no menu of ours open.

## `player:open_inventory(inventory)`

Shows them a real inventory, as if they'd opened it: a chest's, another player's, their ender chest. Whatever was on their screen closes.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inventory` | `Inventory` |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline, or the inventory has gone.

```lua
local chest = player:ender_chest()
if chest then
  player:open_inventory(chest)
end
```

## `player:close_inventory()`

Closes whatever container screen they have open: a chest, a project menu, their own inventory.

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:open_dialog(dialog, options?)`

Puts a dialog on their screen: the same as `dialog:open_for(player, options)`. One of the project's dialogs already on their screen is closed (its `close` handlers hear it). A dialog the project doesn't have is an error; a `Dialog` from `nf.dialogs.create` that's gone opens nothing (`false`).

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `dialog` | `string\|Dialog` | Its folder name under `dialogs/`, or a `Dialog` (one from `nf.dialogs.create`, say). |
| `options` (optional) | `DialogOpenOptions` | What to open it with, for this opening only: `context`, input `values`, a `title` or `body` text. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

```lua
player:open_dialog("welcome", { values = { nickname = player:name() } })
```

## `player:close_dialog()`

Takes whatever dialog is on their screen away. When it's one of the project's, its `close` handlers hear it.

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:sidebar()`

Their sidebar: the panel of lines at the right of their screen. Always the same handle for the same player.

**Returns** `Sidebar`

```lua
player:sidebar():set_lines({ "<gold>Coins: " .. coins, "<gray>Round 2" })
```

## `player:border()`

A border of their own, which only they see: the first call gives them one, a copy of their world's, and they see it instead of their world's until `reset_border()` or they leave (it follows them from world to world). The server draws it for them but doesn't enforce it: it doesn't hurt them. `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `WorldBorder?`

```lua
local border = player:border()
if border then
  border:set_center(vec3(100, 0, 100))
  border:set_size(16)
end
```

## `player:has_own_border()`

Whether they see a border of their own (`player:border()`) rather than their world's. `false` when they're offline.

**Returns** `boolean`

## `player:reset_border()`

Takes their own border away: they see their world's again, and the handle `border()` gave answers `nil`.

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline or had no border of their own.

## `player:tab_header()`

The text above the player list (what tab shows), as MiniMessage, or `nil` when there's none or they're offline.

**Returns** `Text?`

## `player:set_tab_header(text)`

Sets the text above the player list.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Text` | MiniMessage; `""` for none. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:tab_footer()`

The text below the player list, as MiniMessage, or `nil` when there's none or they're offline.

**Returns** `Text?`

## `player:set_tab_footer(text)`

Sets the text below the player list.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `Text` | MiniMessage; `""` for none. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:tab_name()`

What the player list (tab) calls them, as MiniMessage: their name unless `set_tab_name` changed it. Their team's prefix and suffix go around it. `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `Text?`

## `player:set_tab_name(text?)`

Changes what the player list calls them, until they leave. Their real name, what chat calls them and what's over their head stay.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` (optional) | `Text` | MiniMessage. Leave it out to go back to their name. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

```lua
player:set_tab_name("<gold>★ " .. player:name())
```

## `player:tab_order()`

Where they come in the player list: higher comes first, and equal ones are sorted as Minecraft sorts them (by team, then name). 0 unless `set_tab_order` changed it; `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `integer?`

## `player:set_tab_order(order)`

Moves them up or down the player list, until they leave.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `order` | `integer` | Higher comes first; default 0. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:is_listed_for(viewer)`

Whether they're in another player's player list (`set_listed_for`). `false` when either is offline.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `viewer` | `Player` | Whose list. |

**Returns** `boolean`

## `player:set_listed_for(viewer, listed)`

Takes them out of another player's player list, or puts them back. Only the list's entry goes: the viewer still sees them in the world and hears them in chat (to hide them altogether, `hide_from`). It stays that way when either of them leaves and comes back, until it's set back.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `viewer` | `Player` | Whose list. |
| `listed` | `boolean` |  |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when either is offline.

```lua
for _, other in ipairs(nf.players.online()) do
  staff:set_listed_for(other, false)
end
```

## `player:below_name()`

The line under their name tag (`set_below_name`), as MiniMessage, or `nil` when they have none (or they're offline).

**Returns** `Text?`

## `player:set_below_name(text?)`

Puts a line of text under their name tag, which every player sees: a rank, their health, a level. It goes when they leave. Minecraft draws this line for every player as soon as anyone has one, so while someone does, players without one show an empty line. It's shown through the scoreboard's below-name slot, which it takes over from anything else showing there.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `text` (optional) | `Text` | MiniMessage. Leave it out to take the line away. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

```lua
player:set_below_name("<gold>VIP")
```

## `player:bossbars()`

The project's boss bars they're among the viewers of (`bossbar:show_to`), offline or not.

**Returns** `BossBar[]`

## `player:resource_pack_status()`

What became of the project's resource pack on their game: `"loaded"`, `"declined"`, `"failed"`, `"pending"` (accepted, still downloading), or `nil` before their game has answered (and when they're offline, or there's no resource pack).

**Returns** `"loaded"\|"declined"\|"failed"\|"pending"\|nil`

## `player:send_block_change(location_or_position, state)`

Shows them a block that isn't there: only their game draws it, and the world doesn't change. It lasts until the real block updates (something changes it, or their game reloads the chunk), or `reset_block`. They can't walk through or stand on it any differently from the real block. A block state the server doesn't have is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `location_or_position` | `Location\|Vec3` | Any point in the block; a bare vector is in their world. |
| `state` | `string` | A block state, as `world:set_block` takes it: `"minecraft:gold_block"`. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

```lua
player:send_block_change(vec3(10, 64, 10), "minecraft:gold_block")
```

## `player:reset_block(location_or_position)`

Shows them the real block again, after `send_block_change`.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `location_or_position` | `Location\|Vec3` | Any point in the block; a bare vector is in their world. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:send_equipment_change(entity, slot, item?)`

Shows them another entity (or player) wearing or holding something it isn't: only their game draws it. It lasts until that entity's equipment really changes, or it goes out of their sight and comes back. An item table with a misspelled field, or an item the server doesn't have, is an error.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entity` | `Entity` | Whose equipment. |
| `slot` | `"main_hand"\|"off_hand"\|"head"\|"chest"\|"legs"\|"feet"\|"body"` | Which slot. |
| `item` (optional) | `Item` | What to show there. Leave it out (or `nil`) to show it empty. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline or the entity has gone.

```lua
player:send_equipment_change(other, "head", { kind = "minecraft:carved_pumpkin" })
```

## `player:camera()`

The entity they're watching through, as a spectator (`set_camera`), or `nil` when they're looking through their own eyes (or offline).

**Returns** `Entity?`

## `player:set_camera(entity?)`

Makes them watch through another entity's eyes, as a spectator does when they click one: they see what it sees until they sneak, or this is called without one. They have to be in spectator mode (`set_game_mode("spectator")`).

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `entity` (optional) | `Entity` | Whose eyes. Leave it out (or `nil`) to give them their own back. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline, not in spectator mode, or the entity has gone.

```lua
player:set_game_mode("spectator")
player:set_camera(boss)
nf.after(100, function()
  player:set_camera()
end)
```

## `player:compass_target()`

Where their compasses point (those that aren't tied to a lodestone): the world's spawn unless `set_compass_target` changed it. `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `Location?`

## `player:set_compass_target(location)`

Points their compasses somewhere: a quest, a base, a meeting point. It lasts until they leave.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `location` | `Location` | Where. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:open_book(pages)`

Opens a book on their screen, as if they'd opened a written book, without giving them one.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pages` | `Text[]` | Each page, MiniMessage, in order. At most 100. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

```lua
player:open_book({
  "<bold>Welcome!</bold>\n\nRead on for the rules.",
  "1. Be kind.\n2. No griefing.",
})
```

## `player:view_distance()`

How many chunks around them the server is sending: the server's own view distance, or what `set_view_distance` asked for, either of them lowered by their own game's setting. A change shows here from the next tick. `nil` when they're offline.

**Returns** `integer?`

## `player:set_view_distance(distance)`

Changes how many chunks around them the server sends, until they leave, from the next tick. Their own game's setting still limits it: `view_distance()` says what they get.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `distance` | `integer` | In chunks, 2 to 32. |

**Returns** `boolean`: `false` when they're offline.

## `player:data()`

Their saved table: one per player, by id, kept across restarts and shared by every script. By convention each module keeps its own part of it under its name (`player:data().shop`), so modules don't trip over each other. It works for someone offline too (`nf.players.get` finds anyone who has joined). It may hold strings, numbers, booleans, tables of them (keyed by strings, or a list numbered from 1), and the API's own values: `Vec3`s, `Location`s, `Item` tables, and `Player`, `Entity`, `Centity` and `World` handles, which come back as the same types (a handle to something gone answers `nil` or `false`, as handles do). Anything else (a function, a `Menu` window, a `Subscription`) is skipped when it's saved, with a line in the log naming where it was (`data.inventory[3]: a function can't be saved`). The table is live: change it and the change is saved, at the next autosave (every five minutes), when the project reloads and when the server stops. It stays in memory across hot reloads rather than being read again, so a script that reloads finds it as it left it. A table that would take more than 1 MiB isn't saved (the last save stands), and the log says so. It's also saved when they leave.

**Returns** `table`

```lua
local shop = player:data().shop or {}
player:data().shop = shop
shop.coins = (shop.coins or 0) + 5
```

## `player:on(event, handler, options?)`

Calls `handler` every time `event` happens to this, until the subscription is cancelled or its script unloads, or this goes away. A handler lives as long as both the script that registered it and the handle it's on. Handlers run in the order they were registered, each with the event object; what one returns means nothing. A handler that errors is logged and the rest still run; after 20 errors in a row it's cancelled. An event this class doesn't have is an error, so a typo is caught where it was made.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event` | `Player.Event` | The event's name. |
| `handler` | `fun(event: Event)` | Called with the event: its payload, plus `stop()`, `cancel()` and the rest of `Event`. |
| `options` (optional) | `EventOptions` | How to listen: `{ every = n }` for `tick`. |

**Returns** `Subscription`: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop listening.

```lua
player:on("chat", function(event)
  log(player:name(), "said", event.message)
end)
```

## `player:once(event, handler)`

Like `player:on`, but the handler runs only the next time the event happens, then stops listening.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `event` | `Player.Event` | The event's name. |
| `handler` | `fun(event: Event)` | Called with the event. |

**Returns** `Subscription`: Call `:cancel()` on it to stop waiting before then.
